description: Single pre-registered curve-intrinsic candidate for theta_binding: the Tate/multiplicative period theta_cand = 2 pi Im(tau_E) of the color E_q (torus-calibrated: theta_torus = 2 log q0 = 2 pi Im(tau_torus)). Decisive q-sensitivity test at q=1 vs q0: theta_binding(q) moves with q but a single-curve invariant of the barely-deformed color E_q (j: 128->129.86) does not. tau_E via m=(e2-e3)/(e1-e3), validated by kleinj(tau)=j.
discipline: no fit; mpmath 30dps; ONE pre-registered principled candidate (2 pi Im tau_E), reported hit/miss; tau_E independently validated by the Klein j-function. Decisive q-slope comparison rather than a single-point coincidence.
verdict: INTRINSIC MISS (scope-(a) on the principled candidate): tau_E is validated (kleinj*1728=j to <1e-6), but the torus-calibrated candidate theta_cand = 2 pi Im(tau_E) = 5.846981567 misses theta_binding = 0.7814539438 at q0 (6.5x), and its q-slope (1.76e-03) is ~6x flatter than theta_binding's (1.01e-02). Reason: Im(tau_E)~0.93 -> the color E_q is GENERIC, not near the Tate/cusp regime where the torus calibration (theta_torus=2 pi Im tau_torus, Im~0.03) lives. Scope (a): rules out THIS principled candidate, not every intrinsic invariant (a j-tuned one would be fishing). With the monodromy (integer-trace) and transport (too-small) negatives, the geometric origin of theta_binding is NOT a color-E_q period -- it points to the W_lambda-side Plancherel/MTC localization (keystone residual i, the already-open frontier). No fit; nothing wired.
